thread:
alex: Heads-up: we need to land a concrete telemetry + dashboard contract for the private/VPC export agent. We want the console dashboards (quota, routing, perf) to work the same for hosted + private, but the agent has firewall/KMS constraints that affect what we can ship. Need cross-team sync on fields, versions, and rollout UX.

maria: +1. Can we list the minimum metrics the runtime must emit? we should keep the agent payload small (customers worry about egress).

sam: From product/console POV we need per-customer: latency p50/p95, tokens_in, tokens_out, token_cost_estimate, model_variant, request_route (routing policy id), and a binary flag private:true/false. Also a small error taxonomy (auth, quota, fallback).

kevin: For billing/analytics the important ones are tokens_in, tokens_out, model_id, and a per-request cost bucket (nanocost). If agent can't report raw tokens for privacy reasons, we need aggregates per-minute. Is per-minute agg acceptable?

maria: per-minute aggregates are fine. Proposal: agent can emit either raw_events (low volume) or aggregates: {window_start, window_seconds, requests, tokens_in, tokens_out, avg_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio}. That's compact and firewall-friendly.

olivia: Security note: anything leaving VPC must be wrapped with envelope encryption using customer KMS or our brokered KMS if customer allows. Also include an audit_log_id header for replayability. We also need to know the egress IPs so customers can firewall allowlist.

alex: Good call. We should version the schema: telemetry_v1 (current), telemetry_v2 (this contract). Add "kms_mode": "customer|redwood|none" and "audit_log_id" fields.

sam: For dashboards, we need routing policy labels included so we can show per-policy SLOs (e.g., low-cost vs low-latency routing). Field name: routing_policy_id and optional routing_policy_name. UI will fallback to id if name missing.

maria: Example aggregate payload I'm proposing (JSON):
```
{
  "schema": "telemetry_v2",
  "customer_id": "cust_123",
  "window_start": "2026-03-20T15:32:00Z",
  "window_seconds": 60,
  "requests": 42,
  "tokens_in": 12000,
  "tokens_out": 11800,
  "avg_latency_ms": 190,
  "p95_latency_ms": 520,
  "kv_cache_hit_ratio": 0.72,
  "routing_policy_id": "rp-lowcost-1",
  "model_variant": "gptx-3-8q",
  "kms_mode": "customer",
  "audit_log_id": "audit-2026-03-20-az1-44"
}
```

kevin: That looks good. One ask: also include a small "cost_estimate_cents" field so console can render dollar numbers without re-computing. Keep it optional.

olivia: For KMS we need a header with encrypted envelope metadata; prefer a separate metadata handshake endpoint on our control plane so the agent never sends raw keys in the same payload. We'll document a two-step: POST /handshake -> get upload_token, then POST /telemetry?token=upload_token. upload_token TTL short.

alex: Regarding firewall: two options for customers — allowlist static egress IPs (we publish a range) OR allow agent to push to a regional S3-compatible endpoint (signed uploads). We should support both. Which teams own publishing the IP ranges? @maria?

maria: eng-infra will publish the ranges, yes. We'll coordinate with networking for region mapping. Also we need a fallback when firewall blocks: agent should queue locally and surface a console signal (agent status metric) so customers can see export_backlog_count.

sam: UX/Rollout notes: in console we want a "telemetry readiness" banner per-tenant showing: schema version detected, last successful upload, export_backlog_count, kms_mode. When we rollout telemetry_v2, console should gracefully fall back to telemetry_v1 for tenants that don't upgrade their agent. Flag toggle in dev feature-flagging for 4 weeks.

kevin: For dashboards, we want a couple of derived metrics computed server-side: cost per 1k tokens, median batch_size, and fallback_rate. Will compute once we receive aggregates. Need to ensure fields support those calculations.

maria: Implementation concerns: agent binary size and CPU. Keep aggregates simple; avoid heavy histograms. If customers want fine-grained latency histograms, we'll do an opt-in raw_events route but that's behind a customer switch.

olivia: Audit-hook: every handshake and telemetry upload must be logged in our audit trail with the audit_log_id and an HMAC of the payload. This allows offline verification for compliance. We'll need to include HMAC metadata in the upload headers.

alex: Next steps:
- maria: draft the telemetry_v2 schema + small swagger for handshake/upload (due Tue)
- sam: mock console banners/graph mapping + fallback UX (due Wed)
- kevin: list derived metrics and queries for dashboards (due Wed)
- olivia: draft KMS/audit header spec + HMAC scheme (due Tue)
- ops: publish egress IP ranges and S3 endpoints (maria will coordinate)

sam: Also let's add a short migration plan for customers: agent versions that support telemetry_v2 and a rollout flag. We should notify solutions-eng before turning on auto-aggregation.

maria: I'll put the draft in the design doc and ping this thread when ready. tagging @kevin @olivia for review when done.

deploy-bot: Reminder: created doc "telemetry/v2-agent-export-spec.md" in internal drive (link: https://redwood.internal/telemetry/v2-agent-export-spec)

alex: Thanks everyone — this is helpful. We'll meet tomorrow 10am if needed.
